title: What Is RxJS? Observables and Reactive Thinking
summary: What an Observable is, how it differs from a Promise, and why RxJS models clicks, HTTP responses, and timers as one thing: a stream of values that arrive over time.

title: Creating Observables
summary: Turn any source into a stream with RxJS's creation functions — of, from, fromEvent, interval, timer, range, EMPTY, throwError, and defer — and know which ones complete and which run forever.

title: Subscribing: Observers and Subscriptions
summary: Nothing happens until you subscribe. Learn the Observer's next/error/complete callbacks, what subscribe() returns, and how to tear a subscription down with unsubscribe().

title: The Observable Lifecycle and Contract
summary: The rules every Observable follows: lazy, unicast-by-default execution, the next*(error|complete)? grammar, why terminal notifications stop the stream, and how teardown runs.

title: The pipe() Function and Pipeable Operators
summary: Operators are the heart of RxJS. Learn how pipe() composes pure, pipeable operators into a left-to-right transformation pipeline without mutating the source Observable.

title: Transforming Values: map, tap, and scan
summary: Reshape each emission with map, run side effects with tap, and accumulate state across emissions with scan — the everyday transformation operators, plus how scan differs from reduce.

title: Filtering Values: filter, take, first, and friends
summary: Let through only what you want and stop when you're done: filter, take, takeWhile, takeLast, skip, first, and last — including which ones complete the stream and which throw on empty.

title: Rate-Limiting Time: debounceTime, throttleTime, and distinctUntilChanged
summary: Tame noisy streams like keystrokes and scroll events with debounceTime, throttleTime, auditTime, and sampleTime, and drop repeats with distinctUntilChanged.

title: Higher-Order Observables: mergeMap, concatMap, switchMap, exhaustMap
summary: When each value maps to another Observable you get a stream of streams. Master the four flattening operators — and how switchMap cancels, concatMap queues, mergeMap parallelizes, and exhaustMap ignores.

title: Combining Latest Values: combineLatest and withLatestFrom
summary: Derive state from several streams at once. combineLatest emits when any input changes; withLatestFrom samples other streams only when the primary one fires.

title: Joining Streams: merge, concat, zip, forkJoin, and race
summary: Put streams together: merge interleaves, concat runs in sequence, zip pairs by index, forkJoin waits for all to finish, and race picks the first to emit.

title: Subjects: Subject, BehaviorSubject, ReplaySubject, AsyncSubject
summary: A Subject is both an Observable and an Observer — the multicast bridge for pushing values into a stream. Learn the four Subject types and when each fits.

title: Multicasting: Hot vs Cold, share, and shareReplay
summary: Why each subscriber to a cold Observable gets its own run, how to share one execution across many subscribers with share() and shareReplay(), and the refCount pitfall to avoid.

title: Error Handling: catchError, retry, and throwError
summary: Errors are terminal in RxJS. Recover with catchError, retry transient failures (with backoff), raise your own errors with throwError, and understand why a thrown error kills the stream.

title: Completion and Cleanup: finalize, takeUntil, and timeout
summary: Control when streams end and always clean up: complete on a signal with takeUntil, run teardown with finalize, guard slow sources with timeout, and handle empty streams with defaultIfEmpty.

title: Flattening Strategies in Depth: mergeAll, concatAll, switchAll, exhaustAll
summary: Go under the hood of flattening: the *All operators, how the *Map operators equal map + *All, concurrency limits on mergeMap/mergeAll, and how to choose the right strategy every time.

title: Schedulers and Concurrency
summary: Schedulers decide when and on what context work runs. Compare asyncScheduler, asapScheduler, queueScheduler, and animationFrameScheduler, and use observeOn/subscribeOn deliberately.

title: Marble Testing with the TestScheduler
summary: Test time-based streams deterministically. Learn marble-diagram syntax, the TestScheduler's run() helper, and how to assert emissions and subscriptions with virtual time.

title: Building Custom Operators
summary: An operator is just a function from Observable to Observable. Build reusable operators by composing existing ones with pipe(), and go lower-level with the Observable constructor when you must.

title: Buffering, Windowing, and Grouping
summary: Batch and partition streams: collect emissions with bufferTime/bufferCount, slice them into child Observables with windowing, and split by key with groupBy.

title: Memory Management and Anti-Patterns
summary: Subscriptions that never end are leaks. Learn the takeUntil pattern, why nested subscribes are an anti-pattern, the shareReplay leak, and disciplined unsubscription strategies.

title: Real-World Patterns and Async Interop
summary: Assemble what you've learned into production patterns — typeahead search, polling, retry-with-backoff, and caching with shareReplay — and bridge to Promises with firstValueFrom/lastValueFrom.
